title: Compatible finite-reduction morphisms lift into a complete target
statement: Let X,A,J,U be as in [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons], with A Noetherian. Let T,M in D(B_X|U), and assume only that M is locally complete for the residue kernel. Then the map Hom(T,M) -> sections(G), g sent to (R_n(g))_n, for the actual normalized finite-reduction Hom tower G of [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons], is surjective. No perfectness or boundedness of T and no Mittag-Leffler hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 0940 and 0941, representable exactness of the Roos triangle; Tag 09C6, construction of the morphism from compatible finite reductions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adic-complete-reduction-cone] to M. For a section s of the actual reduction Hom tower, take adj_n(s_n) followed by e_n inverse. The successor equality in that lemma and the section equation give a compatible family of maps T -> F_n.

Lift that family along the homotopy-limit cone. In its Roos triangle lift the product tuple; its composite with 1-shift vanishes after every product projection by compatibility. Triangle.coyoneda_exact₂ produces the map into the cone point. Product projection equations recover every component. This proves the surjective half of the Milnor Hom sequence without any finiteness hypothesis.

Compose the lifted map with eM to obtain g:T -> M. The specified leg equalities and naturality of each scalar adjunction unit show adj_n(R_n(g)) = adj_n(s_n). Injectivity of the adjunction equivalence gives R_n(g)=s_n for every n. Extensionality of sections proves the stated surjectivity.
